newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 7.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
HOUSE WILL DECIDE GOVERNOR'S FATE

The future of the Uttar Pradesh governor will be decided by parliament's lower house, the prime minister said. The house would debate the law and order situation in the state and vote on the subject. However, with the Congress party deciding to side with the government on the motion sponsored by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the scheduled debate could end up taking the governor temporarily off the hook. The two Left constituents of the ruling coalition also made it known that they would not support the motion since they did not want to be clubbed with the BJP.
The Economic Times
PANEL FOR ABOLITION OF PAR VALUE; LOCK-IN PERIOD REDUCED

The primary market advisory panel set up by the bourse regulator (SEBI) suggested the abolition of par value of shares. It also suggested reducing the lock-in period for promoters' holdings acquired through public or preferential issues. The panel's recommendations would need to be examined by the department of company affairs and receive SEBI's approval before coming into force. The panel, however, decided to retain the regulation prescribing minimum subscription of 90 percent for an issue to be declared successful.
HOUSE PANEL PITCHES FOR OVERHAUL OF PRIMARY MARKET

The parliamentary committee on finance recommended sweeping changes in the working of the capital market. In its first draft report, the committee recommended against the introduction of options and futures, recommended raising investment limits of insurance companies from five percent to 10 percent and reducing the long-term capital gains tax for individuals to 10 percent to bring them at par with foreign institutional investors.
CONSUMER GOODS IMPORT TO BE FURTHER LIBERALISED

The import of consumer goods would be further liberalised. In an interview the finance minister said this had become necessary in order to ease the pressure on the apex bank (RBI) to buy dollars for keeping the rupee from appreciating. The minister said he would discuss the issue with the RBI on March 15. This indicated that the measures for liberalising consumer goods imports might come on April 1, 1997 when the new export-import policy was announced.
Financial Express
CALLS ZOOM, GILTS CRASH AS APEX BANK DRAINS 30.65 BLN RUPEES

The government securities market crashed on tight liquidity consequent to the apex bank sucking out 30.65 billion rupees through its repo window and the spectre of about 55 billion rupee advance tax payments looming over the system. Call rates rose to 6.75 percent, registering a rise of over 100 percent over the previous closing. Consequently, foreign banks lost the arbitrage advantage that had accrued to them ever since the apex bank opened the repo window.
FULL RUPEE CONVERTIBILITY SOON: PRIME MINISTER

The prime minister said the country would move towards full convertibility of the rupee as soon as possible. He said the rupee was made convertible on the current account and a measure of convertibility introduced in the capital account. He admitted the infrastructure sector was proving to be inadequate for a rapidly transforming economy, like India. Reforms on this front were, therefore, high on the government's agenda, he added.
RESCHEDULING OF LOANS BY FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS BANNED

The apex bank (RBI) would not allow financial institutions to reschedule loans as a means to improve the quality of their assets. At the same time, the RBI liberally revised the definition of non-performing assets. Accordingly, from the current fiscal an institution's asset may be treated as non-performing if interest was due for more than 180 days and/or the principal was due for more than 365 days, an RBI official said.
Business Standard
CORPORATES LINE UP $6 BLN GDR ISSUES

The Indian GDR markets would witness fresh activity, with several state owned firms (PSUs) and some select corporates tapping the markets over the next six to eight months. The main offerings would be that of the PSUs. Marketmen said very few Indian corporates, who deferred plans for GDR offerings in 1996, would come back immediately to tap the markets. Foreign institutional investors and fund managers estimated nearly $6 billion, including conversions, could be raised through this route. However, this would mainly be through large PSU GDR issues which would dilute the impact of the smaller-sized private sector offerings.
INVESTORS IN CORE SECTOR NO LONGER NEED TAX HAVEN ROUTE

Overseas investors funding infrastructure sector projects would no longer have to route funds through Mauritius and other tax havens. Abolition of the tax on dividends in the hands of shareholders and the tax exemption on long-term capital gains for companies investing in infrastructure has nullified the tax havens' advantages because of their avoidance treaties with India. A majority of overseas investors preferred to come to India through investment subsidiaries floated in tax havens to minimise the tax implications on repatriated profits drawing benefits from the tax treaties.
$1 BILLION PROJECTS TO MAKE CLEANER DIESEL

The Public Investment Board cleared all nine diesel hydro desulphurisation (DHDS) units with an estimated project cost of over $1.67 billion. The DHDS process yields superior quality diesel with low sulphur content. Four of these were being set up by Indian Oil Corporation, two by Hindustan Petroleum Corporation and one each by Bharat Petroleum Corporation, Cochin Refineries and Madras Refineries. The projects would now be sent for cabinet approval.
BOURSE INDEX SHEDS 64 POINTS ON CORRECTION

The Bombay bourse index shed 64.95 points to close at 3876.04 points against the previous close of 3940.99. Market sources attributed the slump to an impending technical correction. A correction of 60 odd points was very much round the corner with those who entered the market at lower levels deciding to book profits, a leading dealer said. As of now, foreign institutional investors were not very active, but enquiries were coming in. However, the market was strong and should find support around the 3,850 level, he added.
The Observer
VSNL TO HAVE 18.9 MLN SHARES ON OFFER

The pricing of Videsh Sanchar Nigam's (VSNL) massive global depository receipts (GDR) issue would be announced on March 24, 1997. It would be listed on the London bourse the following day. The international offering was for 18.9 million shares in the form of 37.8 million GDRs, representing one-half of one equity share. The offer comprised 3.9 million shares being offered by the government, VSNL's largest shareholder and upto a maximum of 15 million new shares being issued by the company.
STATE OWNED BANKS SET TO LOWER PRIME LENDING RATE

Leading state-owned banks would lower their prime lending rates by 0.5-1 percent, after the apex bank's (RBI) announcement of the slack season credit policy in April. Banking sources said a consensus was reached among most of the banks in this regard. This followed the steps taken by the government in the budget with regard to various incentives to corporates. However, since the banks were expecting a cut in the cash reserve ratio in the slack season credit policy, the reduction of the lending rate would await the announcement of the credit policy by the apex bank.
Business Line
ABNI SCOUNTING FOR NEW INDIAN PARTNER

Asian Business News India (ABNI), the business news television channel owned by Dow Jones, would have a new partner for its Indian operations soon. This follows its break-up with the Hinduja-owned IndusInd media. The Mauritius based ABNI was looking for an Indian partner to fill the slot vacated by the Hinduja group in the $3 million venture. Hindujas had 26 percent equity stake and were marketing the channel in India. TV-18, a Delhi-based television software company, holds 23 percent equity of ABNI and was producing software for the channel from India.
